findings.text: The sheets now hold every row the registers count: Requirements 640, Evidence 368, Operational issues 44, Assessment findings 313 (its own sheet), so the workbook and the registers agree.
findings.why: The prototype holds 117 requirements in full; the other rows are filled in from each control's counts, as the sheet says.

extra.text: In the SCTM, a row's number opens that row's record preview beside the workbook; every record in a cell opens its own: a finding its finding, evidence its artifact.
The workbook is Controls' spreadsheet view: Controls offers Open as spreadsheet in its header, and the workbook's back link and Close return to Controls.
Posture's Columns switches between control families and the 14 resiliency techniques of SP 800-160 Vol. 2; by technique, cells count the boundary's objectives, issues and risks.
extra.why: Partly: by technique reads the authorization boundary only; the snapshot places objectives on the elements inside it by control family alone.

extra.text: A link naming an SSP section (Shown in SSP section 13, §9, §12) opens the SSP editor at that section, not at its top.
New plan creates the draft: listed on Plans as revision 1, Draft, with its preview; Create draft opens its editor, and what is written there stays.

Shown twice (↗ opens a page repeating the preview): review queue item, ATT&CK technique, asset, interconnection, agent run, authorization decision, another program's gate. WS-X90's gates open their Lifecycle page instead.
extra.why: Not folded: Josef has not decided. Each preview's ↗ opens a page repeating 92–99% of its words; assets 67–72%.

extra.text: Posture's callout no longer shows a rotated copy of its sentence beside the icon (lane F's edit wrote it into the icon too).
